back: Forward: evaluate and record the graph. Backward: seed $\bar L=1$ and visit nodes in reverse topological order, accumulating `parent.grad += local_derivative * node.grad`.
Forward: one pass per input (a Jacobian column). Reverse: one pass per output (a row). Loss is scalar, so reverse.
A node used by several consumers receives one contribution per path; they must sum (multivariate chain rule).
Same forward in float64 with `requires_grad=True`, call `.backward()`, compare `.grad` to your gradients; expect ~1e-10.
Gradients accumulate (zero them); in-place ops can break backward; `detach`/`no_grad` cut the graph; only leaves get `.grad`.
